author: EmuCore - Hub
title: Making a PS2 Game LIVE #1 - Setup (C Game Development on PS2SDK)
summary: The first episode of a public PS2 homebrew series records the complete starting loop: create a C project around PS2SDK, compile a minimal program, and run the result in an emulator with the exact source revision linked.

blocks.text: Instead of beginning from a mature engine, this eighty-seven-minute stream preserves the fragile first milestone of native development. The project is assembled around PS2SDK, enough C code is introduced to produce a build, and the artifact is launched in an emulator. That narrow scope makes it useful historical documentation of the community toolchain: repository layout, compiler environment and execution loop must all work before graphics or gameplay systems matter. The description links directly to the source tree for this specific stream.

An emulator boot confirms that the generated program can enter one development environment; it does not prove behavior on retail hardware or document every host operating system. The public description also omits pinned toolchain versions, emulator build and a concise dependency list, so reproducing an old stream may require reading its repository history. Use the session to understand the setup sequence and failure points. For a current project, follow maintained PS2SDK documentation and validate on hardware before depending on timing-sensitive behavior.
